newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska says one-off gain boosts profit.
newsitem.headline: Skanska says one-off gain boosts profit.

text.p: Swedish construction and real estate group Skanska on Friday posted a jump in nine-month profits, bolstered by a substantial one-off gain, saying the Swedish construction market was showing little improvement.
Skanska said its income after financial items rose to 3.44 billion crowns from 2.05 billion. Order bookings totalled 36.45 billion crowns compared with 27.36 billion in the year-ago period.

The profit after financial items included a 1.76 billion crown capital gain mostly from the sale of Skanska's entire stake in hydroelectric power and timber company Graninge in the first half of the year.
Skanska said the Swedish housing construction market, although showing signs of picking up in the first half of 1996, remained slow.
"The downturn in the Swedish constuction market, especially related to housing constuction, bottomed out last year," Skanska said in its nine-month results statement.
"Despite a slight upturn during the first half of 1996, however, the level of residential construction remains very low, while road and civil engineering investments are showing signs of a slowdown."

Order bookings in Skanska's international construction operations in the period rose 31.3 percent to 14.67 billion crowns. This was helped in particular by the U.S. market in the third quarter, it said.
"Growth was especially strong in Skanska's American operation and this was the main factor behind the increase."
"In Russia, project demand is now higher following the presidential election," Skanska said.
